title: A contrast test that caught a real bug on its first run
summary: A hand-checked design rule became a CI test. Its first run caught a dark-mode badge at 3.5:1, fixed in the same PR.
shows: Rules become automated checks, and checks catch real problems before readers do.

steps.label: verified
steps.text: Theme colors were checked by hand, so nothing stopped a later tweak from failing contrast (backlog d4).

steps.label: recommendation
steps.text: Picked first in the CEO's mini-sprint at priority 60: cheap, low risk, protects earlier contrast work.

steps.label: verified
steps.text: Acceptance criteria written before building: every text color pair in both themes, 4.5:1 minimum, fix any failure in the same PR.

steps.label: verified
steps.text: Built a unit test that computes contrast for every theme text color and fails CI below 4.5:1.

steps.label: verified
steps.text: The test's first run flagged the dark-mode red badge at 3.5:1. It was fixed to 7.5:1 in the same PR.

steps.label: verified
steps.text: Polish, Shield, Lens, Trial, and Coordinator signed off. Trial confirmed a deliberately bad color makes the test fail.

outcome: Merged as PR #31. The test now runs on every pull request.

title: Filters without scripts: when the first design hit our own guardrail
summary: The first filter design used form inputs, which the team's own CI bans. Instead of loosening the check, the team rebuilt the filters with plain links.
shows: Guardrails hold even when they slow the team down, and limits are written down, not hidden.

steps.label: verified
steps.text: What's new and Known issues couldn't be narrowed to one area like email (backlog d1).

steps.label: verified
steps.text: Set the constraint up front: filters stay CSS-only, because check.py bans scripts and that ban stays.

steps.label: verified
steps.text: The first design used radio buttons and hit check.py's ban on form inputs.

steps.label: recommendation
steps.text: Rebuilt with anchor links, :target, and :has() instead of loosening the check.

steps.label: verified
steps.text: Checked the email filter shows only email items, the default shows all 17, and every chip works by keyboard.

steps.label: hypothesis
steps.text: Known gap: screen readers aren't told which chip is active. Worth revisiting only if the script ban ever changes.

outcome: Merged as PR #33 with the limit noted in the review.

title: Moving the team's rules from prose into code
summary: After Ryno shared @poteto's post on trusting agents, the team counted its own mistakes, built a helper so the right path is the default, and cut the rules the helper and CI now enforce.
shows: Mistakes are counted from real records, then fixed in tools instead of more instructions.

steps.label: verified
steps.text: Ryno's pitch i30: code first, then CI, minimal prose, least human review. Atlas leads the audit, Critic challenges it, Coordinator scores it.

steps.label: verified
steps.text: 31 of 247 CI runs had failed. Top agent pitfalls: sign-offs picked by hand (4 PRs), values typed by hand (8), wrong branch type (2 PRs).

steps.label: hypothesis
steps.text: Weakest assumption: that the bots will use the helper. Cut prose only where CI or the helper enforces the rule.

steps.label: verified
steps.text: Built scripts/bot.py. A test ran its branch choice through CI's own path rule on 175 path mixes, and all passed.

steps.label: verified
steps.text: Schema-checked loaders in build.py. On its first use, the helper refused a chat note over 280 characters before it was written.

steps.label: verified
steps.text: Cut 7 prose rule passages that code or CI now enforces. Judgment calls stayed in prose.

outcome: Merged as #56 to #59. Every PR since has been opened with scripts/bot.py.
